topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture framing by establishing the importance and complexity of the complement system.

topics.label: Complement system fundamentals and C3 activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the foundational architecture of the complement system, including its primary functions, naming conventions, and the central role of C3.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways and threshold
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three activation pathways of complement and how they generate convertases to reach the trigger threshold.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the primary downstream effector functions through which complement eliminates pathogens and coordinates immune defense.

topics.label: Regulation of complement on host cells
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory mechanisms and surface proteins that prevent complement from damaging host tissues.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the distinct clinical phenotypes and disease presentations resulting from deficiencies in specific complement components and regulators.

topics.label: Pathogen complement evasion and medical applications
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic covers the strategies pathogens use to circumvent complement attack and the biomedical applications derived from bacterial evasion proteins.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming session on the adaptive immune system.
